From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

Subject: Contractor logs — access, retention, and SSO provisioning (triage)

Team / Katie —

Following up on the legal request we received from Acme (see ticket JIRA-RED-2247). They want clarity on how contractor activity logs are retained, who can access them, and whether BYOK or KMS controls need to be applied to contractor-related keys. High-level asks:

- Confirm default retention for contractor-generated logs and whether we can offer a short-term carveout for contractors (e.g., 90d) vs. enterprise standard (365d).
- Define who (internal roles) may access contractor logs for forensic or billing reasons; can we gate via SSO groups?
- Clarify whether contractor log streams can be scoped under the customer BYOK envelope (customer-managed keys) or must be under Redwood-managed keys.

I attached a quick retention_matrix_draft.xlsx and a log-schema-proposal.md to help frame options.

Immediate goal: get this triaged across product, security, and ops so we can respond to Acme by EOD Monday. Please reply with recommended approach, blockers, and an owner for each decision.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Katie Park <katie@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:15:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Contractor logs — access, retention, and SSO provisioning (triage)

Thanks Jordan — good framing. A few initial positions from Product/Security: 

1) Retention: default customer-facing retention remains 365 days. For contractors we can offer a temporary carveout (90 days) but only as an account-level policy — not per-individual — to keep complexity down. Any shorter retention for contractors should be flagged in the contract and requires Legal signoff.

2) Access controls: we should gate all contractor log access behind SSO group membership + an "auditor" role in Console. That means we need SCIM sync for customer groups (or RBAC mapping in private deployments). Grace, Ben — what is the ops effort to support SCIM group mapping across Hosted and Dedicated?

3) BYOK/KMS: security preference is to surface contractor streams under the customer's BYOK envelope where the customer explicitly adds a key policy for contractor data. Practically, that will require a small change in our key-lookup flow to accept a data-scope label (e.g., "contractor-logs") when deciding whether to use customer vs. platform key. Implementation ETA: P1 design, P2 implementation in next quarter unless we scope a lighter-weight workaround (tokenized envelope keys).

4) Audit sampling: Legal/Compliance often wants samples for e-discovery. Recommend we provide a documented sample collection flow (w/ masked PII) and a signed process for when raw unmasked logs are shared.

I'm happy to own the product-side decision doc. Jordan — can you confirm Acme's legal point of contact and whether the contract already mentions "contractors" explicitly?

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Product, Security Features
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Katie Park <katie@acmehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:05:30 -0800
Subject: Re: Contractor logs — access, retention, and SSO provisioning (triage)

Jordan & Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Our legal team requires that contractor activity tied to patient data be retained for a minimum of 2 years for auditability; non-PHI contractor logs can be 90 days.
- We cannot put contractor logs under Redwood-managed keys if they contain PHI; BYOK is a must in that case. For non-PHI traces we are OK with platform keys.
- For SSO, we use an external IdP and can expose groups via SCIM; we will need your team to map those groups to roles in Redwood.

I'll loop in Legal if we need to change contract language — Katie Park, Privacy Counsel (katie@acmehealth.com). We appreciate a clear option set and the risks/costs for each.

Best,
Katie

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Katie Park <katie@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:30:45 -0800
Subject: Re: Contractor logs — access, retention, and SSO provisioning (triage)

Quick ops reality check: 

- Storage/cost: moving contractor non-PHI logs to 90d is straightforward. Keeping PHI logs at 2y will add about ~18% storage for this account based on current retention curves — we should surface that to Acme.
- BYOK: we can scope contractor-keyed data under the customer's KMS. We'll need a small flag in ingestion to tag events as "contractor" so the routing layer uses the customer's key. That tagging can be done at the tenant-proxy (low-effort) or by the client (preferred for accuracy).
- SCIM: we support SCIM group sync for Hosted customers already; mapping to internal roles is a config task. For Dedicated/Private deployments we may need a short integration plan.

I attached a quick retention_matrix_draft.xlsx with cost delta columns and an implementation checklist. Proposed owners:
- Product decision doc: Marissa (owner)
- Ops implementation (ingestion tag + KMS routing): Ben (owner)
- Legal/contract updates: Jordan to coordinate with Acme Legal (owner)
- SCIM mapping & deployment config: Grace (owner)

If everyone is aligned, I'll spin up a short tech spec and estimate (3-4 dev sprints for a complete BYOK-for-contractors path; 1 sprint for tagging + doc fallback).

-Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Infrastructure Operations
ben_carter@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Contractor logs — access, retention, and SSO provisioning (triage)

Thanks all — short summary and next steps so we can get Acme a firm reply Monday morning: 

Decisions / asks:
- Retention: default 365d; Acme requires 2y for PHI contractor logs, 90d for non-PHI contractor logs. Legal to confirm exact wording. (Owner: Jordan / Acme Legal)
- Access: require SSO group gating + auditor role mapping. Grace to confirm SCIM mapping plan and rollout steps. (Owner: Grace)
- BYOK: enable BYOK for contractor PHI streams. Ops will implement ingestion tagging + KMS routing. Short-term fallback: customer can request export for e-discovery. (Owner: Ben)
- Product doc: Marissa to draft a one-page decision doc + exception matrix for contract language. Target: first draft by Tue 2026-11-23 COB. (Owner: Marissa)

Action items:
- Jordan: confirm Acme legal POC and ask for sample contract clause (due Mon EOD).
- Marissa: create decision doc and add brief risk/cost table (due Tue COB).
- Ben: put together tech spec and cost delta estimate, include required tagging changes (shared by Mon).
- Grace: SCIM mapping plan and Dedicated deployment notes (shared by Tue).

I'll set a 30-minute sync for Tuesday 11/23 10:00am PT to review drafts — invite to follow. If anyone can't make that slot, say so and propose alternates.

Jordan
